newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady, focus on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady, focus on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar in slow early trading on Tuesday, with operators seen focusing on liquidity, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said trading in the spot market was slow and operators were speculating a higher central bank fixing this afternoon.
"Some operators are seen buying dollars below the 2,330.0 level with the hope of a higher fixing later," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,329.5/30.0 at 0230 GMT against an opening of 2,329.80/30.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,328.60/29.00 and 2,328.0/28.5, respectively.
Dealers said it was difficult to make money from the spot market due to the current narrow trading range.
"It's pretty difficult to get a reasonable spread from the market at present. The swap market is more attractive," another foreign bank dealer said.
He said operators were looking at Bank Dagang Nasional Indonesia (BDNI), which has been appointed the settlement bank for Bank Negara Indonesia's (BNI) share offering.
"It (liquidity) is very dependent on what the bank plans to do with the funds. If it starts buying longer-term swaps then it is not good for liquidity," the local dealer said.
"But we haven't seen that so far. BDNI was only seen buying short-dated swaps," he said. Overnight swap rose to 0.45 points from an opening of 0.35/0.45. Tom/next was at 0.55/0.60 points.
The dealer said rises in short-dated swaps might indicate that the settlement bank might want to unload some funds on the market on Wednesday.
Dealers said longer-term rates were stable.
One-month swap was at 17.50/18.25, two at 33.5/34.5, three at 52.0/52.5 and six at 99.0/100.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention rate at 2,329/2,521 and the conversion rate at 2,329/2,377 on Monday.
